problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [-6,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)=u(x-1)+u\,(x-\frac{1}{2})+u\,(x-\frac{1}{3})+⋯,\,g(x)=u(x+4)+u(x-6),\,h(x)={\begin{aligned}-1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is even} \\ 1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is odd}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌈x⌉$ is the ceiling function.
worked_solution:
Suppose $I⊆R.$ A function $f:I\to R$ is piecewise continuous on $I$ if it is piecewise continuous on every closed and bounded subinterval $[a,b]⊂I.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [-6,\infty ).$ Consider the closed subinterval $x\in [0,1].$ Notice that the function has jump discontinuities at $x=1,\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{3},…,$ so it has infinitely many discontinuities on this closed interval.

- The function $g(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [-6,\infty )$ since it is continuous over $x\in [-6,\infty )$ except at the points $x=-4$ and $x=6,$ where the one-sided limits exist and are finite:

$$
{lim}_{x\to -{4}^{-}}g(x)=0,\,{lim}_{x\to -{4}^{+}}g(x)=1
$$

$$
{lim}_{x\to {6}^{-}}g(x)=1,\,{lim}_{x\to {6}^{+}}g(x)=2
$$

- The function $h(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [-6,\infty ).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=0,1,2,…,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]⊂[-6,\infty )$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042449/assets/9e447c0672628ce8b304726f36885f18661bbba790ae34ca806aaae95a465bbb.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "$g$ and $h$ only."
